content.title: Are Michael B. Jordan and Taylor Russell Dating? Here's Why Fans Think So
content.text: The two were most previously linked to Lori Harvey and Harry Styles, respectively Published on March 13, 2025 09:09PM EDT Michael B. Jordan in Beverly Hills, California, on March 12, 2023; Taylor Russell in New York City on May 6, 2024. Credit : Steve Granitz/FilmMagic; John Shearer/WireImage Are Michael B. Jordan and Taylor Russell embarking on a new romance? The pair were spotted together in London on Sunday, March 9, as seen in footage shared by fan account @tayrussellnew on Instagram. Jordan, 38, and Russell, 30, were dressed casually as they walked side by side along a busy portion of Oxford Street lined by shops, per the video. Reps for the stars did not respond to PEOPLE's requests for comment. The actors are set to star opposite one another in a remake of The Thomas Crown Affair for Amazon MGM Studios that will be released in theaters. Jordan is also directing the project. Jordan has been romantically linked to famous partners in the past, including Kendall Jenner, and most recently Lori Harvey. He and Harvey, 28, went Instagram official with their relationship in January 2021, but had split by June 2022. Lionel Hahn/Getty Following their breakup, the Creed III actor-director admitted he "was lucky enough to have a lot of work" to keep his mind off the matter. "It was an experience for me to grow and learn," Jordan said on CBS Mornings in February 2023. "This is my year. There's so much going on, so many blessings, so many great things." Russell, meanwhile, was most recently linked to pop star Harry Styles. The two first sparked dating rumors in June 2023, but broke up in May 2024. The PEOPLE Puzzler crossword is here! SplashNews Aside from directing and starring in the upcoming Thomas Crown Affair movie, Sinners star Jordan is also set to produce under his Outlier Society banner alongside Elizabeth Raposo, from a script by Drew Pearce (Iron Man 3, The Fall Guy). Producers will also include Marc Toberoff and Patrick McCormick, plus executive producer Alan Trustman, who wrote the original 1968 film starring Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway. Jordan's project — his sophomore directorial effort, following 2023's Creed III — will mark the third iteration of The Thomas Crown Affair on film, after the original and a 1999 remake starring Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo.
